#5586. ICF Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results

âThird Quarter Marks Return to Year-on-Year Revenue Growthâ

âRevenue from Federal Government Clients Increased 3.4% Sequentiallyâ

âMargin Expansion Benefited from Efficient Contract Delivery and Favorable Contract Mixâ

âMaintains 2026 Non-GAAP EPS Guidance Midpoint on Lower Revenueâ

RESTON, Va., Nov. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- ICF (NASDAQ: ICFI), a global consulting and technology services provider, reported results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

John Wasson, chair and chief executive officer, said, "Our third quarter performance demonstrated the return to year-on-year revenue growth that we anticipated would begin in the second half of this year and benefited from our diversified and integrated business model. Revenues from our federal government clients continued to show solid sequential growth in line with our expectations, and revenues from state and local and non-U.S. government clients increased 7.6% and 12.0% year-on-year, respectively.

"A key highlight of the third quarter was our strong margin performance, benefiting from efficient contract delivery and favorable contract mix. Our Adjusted EBITDA margin was 11.5%, expanding by 10 basis points year-on-year and representing a notable sequential increase. Fixed-price contracts accounted for 50.2% of our third quarter revenues, up from 48.7% in the similar period last year, and together with time & material contracts represented 94.3% of this quarter's revenues. We are closely managing corporate costs, while continuing to invest in technology and professional staff to support client programs and capture new business opportunities.

"Third quarter revenues from commercial energy clients were considerably below our expectations due to a confluence of factors, most notably a sharp fall-off in contract add-on activity that historically has bolstered second half revenues in our utility programs category. There was a material increase in political and regulatory pressure on utilities in Q3 to develop affordable solutions for their customers, which has caused a slowdown and/or shift in incremental spending priorities for certain existing utility programs. Also, we experienced slower than expected ramp-ups on new contracts. As a result, ICF's revenues from commercial energy clients are expected to increase at a low- to mid-single-digit rate for 2026. We continue to see commercial energy as a long-term growth driver for ICF. Our year-to-date contract awards have been strong, our win rates are increasing, and we are building a meaningful pipeline in areas where we see utility spending expanding, including audits/weatherization, demand response and virtual power plants.

"This also was a strong quarter for companywide contract awards, which increased 4.5% year-on-year to $746 million. Over 60% of our third quarter awards represented new business, a good indication of how well ICF's capabilities and expertise are aligned with our clients' priorities. Following this solid performance, our business development pipeline stood at $8.2 billion at the end of the third quarter and was well diversified across our client set."

Third Quarter Business Highlights in Key Long-Term Growth Markets

ICF manages over 300 energy efficiency programs for 60 utilities in 28 states. Revenues from this part of the company's commercial energy business were similar to last year's levels due to the near-term challenges described above. We continue to see positive underlying momentum supported by year-to-date contract wins and client demand for our expertise as they address affordability issues together with operational imperatives around electrification and data center requirements. Energy advisory revenues increased 14.1% in the quarter and 10.5% year-to-date, with particular strength in our work on grid engineering and planning, transmission and interconnection, integrated power and gas planning, resource adequacy, technical due diligence, and storage. Additionally, our work with hyperscalers is expanding, and we are advising on a broader set of issues created by the scale of data center development, including energy efficiency, community impacts, power supply and reliability. As anticipated, other commercial energy comparisons declined year-on-year due to the wind-down of several wind energy projects through last year's third quarter.

Commercial energy awards represented approximately 26% of year-to-date contract awards, and commercial energy opportunities represent more than $1.6 billion of our pipeline at the end of the third quarter.

ICF's energy work includes programs for federal and state agencies that provide us with greater insight into the regulatory and stakeholder environment, which strengthens our ability to meet and often exceed the milestones of our commercial energy contracts.

ICF has built out its technology modernization capabilities over the last six years, which in the third quarter represented approximately 50% of our revenues from federal government clients. Over 80% of ICF's technology modernization work is performed under outcome-based, fixed-price contracts, the preferred contract vehicles for government technology projects. Additionally, we continue to align our federal portfolio around administration priorities, with increased focus on expanding our footprint in the defense and national security arena, while building our brand in government-wide application modernization.

While primarily serving federal agency clients, our technology modernization capabilities are deployed across the company's client categories. Technology modernization opportunities represented approximately $2.4 billion of our pipeline at the end of the third quarter.

State and Local Government/Disaster Recovery

The 7.6% revenue growth from state and local government clients in the third quarter illustrates ICF's ability to leverage its deep domain expertise and robust technology capabilities across its client sets. Several of the projects driving growth in this client category include developing and managing energy efficiency programs in the Northeast and California, providing advanced technology solutions to several states and territories, and offering our rural health services.

During the quarter, ICF supported more than 50 active disaster recovery programs in more than 20 states and territories. While we view the disaster management market as a driver of long-term growth, funding delays and the slower pace of major events have constrained near-term activity in this arena. ICF continues to execute substantial rebuilding and mitigation projects utilizing our environmental and climate expertise, and we are helping our clients prepare to take on a larger role in rebuilding and resilience, having significantly increased our on-call contracts with state and local governments. State and local government opportunities represented approximately $1.1 billion of the total pipeline at the end of the third quarter.

Third quarter 2026 total revenue was $470.5 million, up 1.1% from the $465.4 million reported in the third quarter of 2025. Subcontractor and other direct costs were 23.6% of total revenues, compared to 24.2% in last year's third quarter. Gross margin was 38.1%, 50 basis points above the prior year period. Operating income was $43.6 million, up 13.6% from $38.4 million, and operating margin expanded by 100 basis points to 9.3% from 8.3% in the prior year period. Net income totaled $31.7 million, or $1.76 per diluted share, up from net income of $23.8 million, or $1.28 per share reported in the third quarter of 2025, benefiting from a tax rate of 15.0% and a lower share count. In the prior year quarter, the company's tax rate was 22.7%.

Non-GAAP EPS increased 18.6% to $1.98 per share, benefiting from the lower tax rate and share count mentioned above. EBITDA was $53.6 million, up from $52.8 million reported in the year-ago quarter. Adjusted EBITDA was $54.2 million, and Adjusted EBITDA margin on total revenues was 11.5%, compared to 11.4% in the third quarter of 2025.

Cash flows from operations were $35.2 million in this year's third quarter. Excluding restricted cash mainly tied to energy efficiency programs, which fluctuates with the timing of incentive payments to utility customers, operating cash flow was $45.5 million, up from $17.3 million reported in the comparable prior year period. For the first nine months of 2026, cash flows from operations were $131.7 million. Excluding restricted cash, year-to-date operating cash flows were $88.7 million, up from $30.2 million in the first nine months of 2025, on a similarly adjusted basis.

Total backlog was $3.5 billion at the end of the third quarter of 2026. Funded backlog was $1.8 billion, or approximately 52% of the total backlog. The total value of contracts awarded in the 2026 third quarter was $746 million for a quarterly book-to-bill ratio of 1.59 and trailing twelve-month contract awards totaled $2.0 billion for a book-to-bill ratio of 1.11.

Commercial Revenue Third Quarter 2026 Highlights

Commercial revenue was $158.8 million during the quarter, up 1.5% year-over-year.

Key Commercial Contracts Awarded in the Third Quarter of 2026

Government Revenue Third Quarter 2026 Highlights

Revenue from government clients was $311.7 million during the quarter.

Key Government Contracts Awarded in the Third Quarter of 2026

On November 5, 2026, ICF declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.14 per share, payable on January 8, 2027, to shareholders of record on December 4, 2026.

"ICF is on the path to second half year-on-year revenue growth, and we see positive momentum as we head into 2027. The adjusted EBITDA margin expansion we achieved in the third quarter was notable, our new contract awards were strong, and our business development pipeline is robust, all indications of the underlying strength of our business and effective cost management. Additionally, given ICF's diversified portfolio, we see the midterm election results as a tailwind for our business.

"For full year 2026, we are expecting revenues to be similar to 2025 levels, with GAAP EPS of approximately $5.95, inclusive of $.11 of special charges. We are maintaining the midpoint of our Non-GAAP EPS guidance range of $7.10, representing 4.9% year-on-year growth and benefiting from improved margins, a lower interest rate and reduced share count. Operating cash flow is expected to range from $135 million to $150 million, excluding the impact of restricted cash.

"We continue to benefit from the energy of our people, who have shown tremendous dedication and commitment to our clients and embody the strong corporate culture that ICF is known for," Mr. Wasson concluded.

#5585. Ocient raises $100 million as agentic AI drives growth in large-scale analytics

Ocient Inc., the maker of a speedy data analytics platform, today said it has raised $100 million in a Series C funding to expand its agentic artificial intelligence analytics business.

That business is fueled by growing demand from national security organizations and telecommunications providers seeking to analyze massive datasets without sampling. The new round brings the Chicago-based company’s total funding to $260 million.

Ocient said it expects revenue to more than triple in its current fiscal year, which ends in January, after doubling revenue the previous year. The company said the new financing will accelerate delivery of its OcientAIQ Solutions, which enable AI agents and human analysts to query petabyte-scale datasets.

Chief Executive John Morris said much of the growth is coming from new customers in national security and telecommunications, particularly organizations using the platform to consolidate cybersecurity information.

“They’ve been accustomed to having to sample data coming off the network,” Morris said. “They don’t have anything that can handle the ingest rates, nor that can store at an affordable price tens of petabytes of data.”

Ocient’s original business focused on high-performance analytics, but the emergence of AI agents has expanded its potential market. Increasingly, software agents rather than human analysts are querying its systems, driving higher utilization and creating demand for more comprehensive datasets.

The OcientAIQ Unified Data Platform combines ingestion, analytics, governance and agent orchestration. Its architecture minimizes data movement and uses forward error correction instead of conventional replication to provide data protection with reduced storage overhead.

“The architecture is designed not to move data around constantly as most architectures do, and to have nothing replicated,” Morris said.

The company competes with Snowflake Inc., Databricks Inc. and open-source analytics implementations, although its technology frequently complements existing platforms rather than replacing them, the CEO said.

Cybersecurity has emerged as a particularly promising market. Ocient provides the underlying data infrastructure that enables security tools and AI agents to analyze network activity across complete historical datasets, potentially identifying threats that conventional sampling would miss.

However, Morris said the company isn’t positioned as a cybersecurity tool. “We don’t do the detection algorithms and the sort of things that the companies in that space do,” Morris said.

Government and defense customers account for a substantial portion of Ocient’s business. The company recently established a dedicated national security subsidiary to serve those markets.

Morris said the new funding should be sufficient to help Ocient reach breakeven, although he declined to provide a timetable. Ocient plans to direct much of the investment toward hiring sales and customer delivery personnel while continuing engineering development.

The company is also seeing increasing demand for on-premises deployments as customers seek greater control over costs and sensitive information. “Most of our opportunities now are on-prem because they’re either repatriating for cost reasons or for data sovereignty and data protection issues,” Morris said.

The company is also looking to expand geographically, particularly in Europe, Asia-Pacific and Latin America, while pursuing additional cybersecurity customers.

The round was co-led by Boka Capital Ltd. and OCA Ventures LLC, with participation from previous investors Greycroft Partners LLC, In-Q-Tel Inc., Blue Bear Capital LLC, Buoyant Ventures Management LLC, PSP Partners LLC’s PSP Growth fund and Pritzker Group Venture Capital LLC.

The CryptoNews editorial team is composed of seasoned writers specializing in cryptocurrency and blockchain technology. Their expertise ensures comprehensive, accurate, and insightful content for...

Donald Trump crypto empire faces fresh pressure as Republicans lose control of Congress in the 2026 midterms, handing Democrats a sweeping victory. The political setback comes as Trump-linked tokens remain deeply underwater and Justin Sun escalates his legal fight against World Liberty Financial, the WLFI.

Sun is seeking nearly $264,000 in sanctions over alleged failures to disclose the project’s UAE ownership ties, and the midterm defeat gives Democrats greater power to investigate Trump’s administration and scrutinize potential conflicts of interest involving his family’s business interests.

Meanwhile, the market has delivered its own verdict. Official Trump, Melania Meme and WLFI tokens have fallen sharply from their peaks, leaving investors nursing substantial losses.

Discover: The Crypto Presales This Q4 2026

The latest legal pressure comes from Justin Sun, who invested $45 million in WLFI tokens before his relationship with the Trump-backed crypto project deteriorated.

Sun sued World Liberty Financial in April, accusing the company of fraud and unlawfully freezing his tokens. The project later countersued, describing his claims as a “meritless PR stunt.”

Now, the Justin Sun dispute has escalated into a fight over WLFI’s corporate ownership disclosures. Sun alleges World Liberty initially identified Florida as its sole citizenship in federal court. Months later, the company amended its filing to identify 22 entities in its ownership chain, claiming citizenship across Florida, Delaware, Puerto Rico, and the United Arab Emirates.

Last night, my lawyers moved to sanction World Liberty Financial @worldlibertyfi for failing to disclose, until months into my litigation against the company, that it is a citizen of the UAE 🇦🇪 . #WLFI #USD1 For those who are new to this dispute, I was one of World Liberty’s…

The amended disclosure came shortly after an August hearing addressing World Liberty’s attempt to move parts of the dispute into arbitration. Sun argues the company should have disclosed its ownership structure earlier, before his legal team spent months challenging arbitration. He claims the late disclosure could undermine the federal court’s jurisdiction.

The WLFI Sanctions motion seeks nearly $264,000 in legal fees and costs from the company and its attorneys. World Liberty’s lawyers reportedly said they learned about the UAE citizenship after the original filing. The court has not determined whether the company intentionally concealed its ownership ties.

Sun plans to refile his lawsuit in California state court once the sanctions motion is resolved. Nevertheless, this controversy adds another complication for Trump Crypto ventures, whose foreign investment connections have already attracted political scrutiny.

The legal dispute arrives as Trump-linked digital assets remain far below their launch-era highs. The official Trump crypto token reached $73.43 in January 2025 before falling to around $1.50. That leaves TRUMP down 98% from its peak.

Melania Meme, the first lady of America-tied meme coin, has suffered an even steeper decline. The token previously reached approximately $13.05 but has since traded near seven cents, representing a loss exceeding 99%.

WLFI has also retreated from its all-time high near $0.33 to roughly five cents. Its fully diluted valuation remains substantial, but its market price reflects a sharp reversal from launch expectations.

The downturn has left Trump crypto investors facing losses while the project’s political and legal connections draw renewed attention.

World Liberty also operates USD1, its dollar-pegged stablecoin, which has grown into a major part of the project’s business. The company’s financial and ownership structure could receive greater scrutiny as Democrats prepare to take control of Congress.

The midterm results have not triggered investigations into Trump crypto ventures, but Democrats will gain subpoena power and greater influence over congressional oversight once the new Congress convenes.

The Trump crypto story is no longer just about political branding and token launches. It is increasingly about investor losses, corporate transparency, and the legal consequences of operating a business tied to the presidency.

#5581. IBM, AMD and Oak Ridge join forces to launch quantum computing error-correction platform

IBM Corp., Advanced Micro Devices Inc. and the Quantum Science Center at Oak Ridge National Laboratory today announced a new quantum error-correction platform that integrates quantum and high-performance computing.

Gaining high performance and correctness in quantum computing requires protecting quantum information from noise. In many cases, researchers have paired quantum computers with classical computers to achieve superior performance for running industry-relevant problems. The challenge today is scaling up these advances with classical computing.

Today’s physical quantum qubits make errors roughly once every few hundred operations. Without correction, errors compound rapidly, rendering long or complex calculations completely untenable. Game-changing algorithms such as Shor’s algorithm for factoring or for molecular-scale simulations in chemistry require billions of error-free operations.

This launch uses a co-design platform for quantum error correction using IBM’s quantum computers, including the 120-qubit Nighthawk with ORNL’s Umbra High-Performance Computing system powered by AMD’s Instinct MI355X graphics processing units and 5th Gen EPYC central processing units.

“ORNL’s strength in high-performance computing, combined with the expertise of our QSC partners – like IBM and AMD – creates an opportunity to push the boundaries of what is possible,” said Director of the Quantum Science Center Travis Humble. “With Umbra, we will now test new ideas, evaluate approaches at scale, and build the foundation for more reliable quantum computers.”

Jay Gambetta, an IBM Fellow and director of IBM Research, added that the biggest contributor to today’s research is no longer whether error correction will work on quantum hardware, but how to accelerate and optimize it to build systems scientists can use to tackle problems.

IBM said the Nighthawk’s square-lattice connectivity enables industry-leading speed and real-time control to test error-correction techniques. GPU accelerators, such as AMD’s nodes in the Umbra system, can help with this fine-tuning. The co-design platform connected at Oak Ridge will help explore quantum as part of a broader artificial intelligence and scientific computing infrastructure.

“This new co-design platform for quantum error correction allows us to evaluate different approaches and determine the architectures, software and workflows that will scale,” said Gambetta.

Researchers can measure qubits mid-calculation and act on the results in real time, set the exact timing for the signals that protect the qubits from noise, and see exactly what the hardware ran while working with raw measurement signals. This will provide error-correction research with the raw data needed for the next generation of approaches to build sophisticated capabilities for large systems running real code.

Earlier this year, IBM and ORNL unveiled results showing how workloads running on both quantum and classical computers and the Frontier supercomputer can simulate real magnetic materials and calculate molecular configurations of a promising material for fusion fuel.

The simulation of magnetic materials could lead to breakthroughs in superconductors, more efficient batteries and novel drugs. A promising fusion fuel could provide a stepping stone to abundant energy superior to nuclear fission, which powers current nuclear power plants.

#5579. Cryoport Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

NASHVILLE, Tenn., Nov. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Cryoport, Inc. (NASDAQ: CYRX) ("Cryoport" or the "Company"), a leading global provider of integrated temperature-controlled supply chain solutions for the life sciences, today announced financial results for its third quarter (Q3) and first nine months (9M) of 2026.

Jerrell Shelton, CEO of Cryoport, stated, "Cryoport delivered third quarter revenue of $50.2 million, reflecting continued momentum across our core cell and gene therapy (CGT) business. Revenue from commercial CGT clients increased 20% year over year, BioStorage/BioServices revenue expanded 25%, and total Life Sciences Services revenue grew 18%, underscoring the strength of our integrated platform and the growing demand for our solutions. These results reflect both the increasing number of patients worldwide receiving CGT treatments and the continued adoption of our end-to-end temperature-controlled supply chain solutions. We also achieved 8% year over year growth in Life Sciences Products revenue, supported by MVE Biological Solutions' (MVE) position as the global market leader in cryogenic systems.

"During the quarter, we further strengthened our leadership position within the CGT ecosystem, ending the period supporting 23 commercial therapies and a record of 788 clinical trials worldwide. Our integrated platform, disciplined execution, and growing utilization of our Global Supply Chain Center Network continue to enhance scalability and operating leverage, advancing our progress toward sustained profitability. This momentum was reflected in our positive adjusted EBITDA of $1.1 million for the quarter, representing another important milestone in our pathway to profitability initiative.

"Our strong year-to-date performance, combined with expanding support of commercial therapies, deepening customer relationships, a robust clinical trial pipeline, and continued demand for MVE's industry-leading products, gives us confidence in our outlook. As a result, we are increasing our full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $197 million to $199 million," concluded Mr. Shelton.

#5578. Exclusive: StrongestLayer launches tools to verify payment requests and block hidden AI instructions

Artificial intelligence email security startup StrongestLayer Inc. today launched two products aimed at email that can move money or manipulate an AI assistant.

The first product, Intent Workflows, can hold payment, payroll and executive account requests for verification before anyone acts on them. Alongside it comes AI Instruction Intercept, which stops hidden instructions in a message before an assistant such as Microsoft Corp.’s Microsoft 365 Copilot reads them

Intent Workflows targets attacks that carry no malware or suspicious link. In vendor email compromise, a criminal takes over a real supplier’s mailbox and sends new bank details inside an existing thread.

StrongestLayer went through 32,052 attacks that got past existing defenses at 45 organizations in the second quarter. Only 3.6% were payment or bank-change requests. Under a loss model built on the Factor Analysis of Information Risk framework, that small slice accounted for more than 98% of the estimated financial exposure. Sender authentication checks were little help, since 94% of those messages passed them.

Traditional email security asks whether a message looks bad, according to Alan LeFort, StrongestLayer’s co-founder and chief executive. “The costliest attacks are built to look fine,” he said. His company looks at what a message is trying to make happen, which for a wire transfer means “verifying the action instead of betting on a verdict.”

StrongestLayer’s detection still screens every message. Intent Workflows adds a hold for the smaller set of requests that can’t be reversed, with each customer deciding whether those requests wait for verification or go to the security team or a process owner.

Customers can also let a request through with a policy banner, which appears only on tracked requests and spells out the company’s own rule, such as “Bank change: call the number on file.” Payments in scope are held whatever the verdict, so a hijacked vendor account can’t get one through by sounding legitimate.

The software compares each payment request with the payee’s history, and customers pick the threshold, whether that is every payment or only those over $5,000. If nothing has changed, the payment owner confirms in one click, in Microsoft Teams or by email. Any change, or a new vendor, means a call to a phone number already on file, and the email isn’t released until the outcome is logged.

Payroll changes are verified the same way, and executive password, multifactor authentication and account recovery resets go to the identity or security team first, even when the request comes in through the help desk.

The release also takes on a newer problem. Researchers at Aim Security Ltd. found the EchoLeak flaw in Microsoft 365 Copilot last year, and one crafted email was all it took to get the assistant leaking data.

AI Instruction Intercept reads each message first. A reasoning model checks it for hidden instructions against the customer’s own business context, and only after that does the email reach Copilot, Google LLC’s Gemini or a security classifier. Suspect messages are quarantined by default with an explanation of what each instruction was after.

Email is the one route to an AI assistant that “any outsider can use,” said Joshua Bass, StrongestLayer’s co-founder and chief product officer. He argues the inbox is the first place to stop prompt injection, since all an attacker needs is an address.

Both products are available now for Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace and run alongside a company’s existing email security.

#5577. What real estate agents should watch on Election Day, per NAHB

NAHB’s Ken Wingert on housing and the midterms, from state ballot measures and the ROAD to Housing Act to tariffs, labor and mortgage rates.

Housing may not be on many ballots by name on Nov. 3, but it’s running through nearly every race.

With the midterms set for Tuesday, candidates from both parties are pitching voters on affordability. Lawmakers are campaigning on the recently passed 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, states from California to Massachusetts are voting on measures meant to make building easier, and homebuilders are grappling with tariffs and immigration enforcement that have driven up costs and thinned out job-site crews.

Inman spoke with Ken Wingert, chief advocacy officer at the National Association of Home Builders, about the races and ballot measures NAHB is watching, whether data centers are really competing with housing for land, and what agents should keep an eye on as votes are counted.

Inman: What are two or three outcomes to the midterms you think matter most for housing — on the federal- level and state-level?

Ken Wingert: The overall theme is that this is turning out to be, once again, an affordability election, and housing is at the top of that pain point … because we don’t have enough of it. So regardless of who controls Congress or who wins the governor’s race in any given state, I think housing will be near or at the top of the agenda going into 2027. That gives us, and other groups you’re probably talking to, a lot of opportunity to advocate for more housing supply.

On specific issues, people are starting to understand that supply matters. You’re seeing ballot initiatives in a number of states aimed at making it easier for builders to build and cutting some of that red tape. Members of Congress are running on the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act. Congress is still debating permitting reform that may pass in the lame-duck session or get kicked to the next Congress.

From a congressional standpoint, if Democrats win at least one chamber, there will probably be more pushback and oversight on issues like tariffs and immigration, which have made it harder for builders to build more housing, or at least more expensive.

Are there specific races that NAHB is watching closely, at the state, federal or local level?

We’re not quite NAR size, but we’re involved in a lot. At the federal level, I think we’ll see how big a wave is, if one materializes, and whether it takes out some folks who have been very helpful on housing over the years.

Financial Services Chairman French Hill will be fine, I think, but he’s in a tighter race than expected. Mike Hill, chairman of the House Financial Services Subcommittee on Housing and Insurance, faces the same challenge. In Michigan, Bill Huizenga is a former Realtor and builder. Sherrod Brown, former chair of the Banking Committee, is potentially coming back to the Senate from Ohio. A lot of folks are watching that race.

But really, at the state level: California has a couple of ballot initiatives, one in particular we’ve been involved with on changes to CEQA, the California Environmental Quality Act. The legislature had made some changes, and this would codify them in state law. In Massachusetts, we’re supporting a ballot initiative that would reduce minimum lot sizes, meaning how big your lot has to be to build on it. And there are a bunch of funding ballot initiatives around the country. All of those aim to increase supply, so we’re keyed in on those state-level races.

I’ve seen candidates from both parties campaigning on the recently passed ROAD to Housing Act. Does that kind of policy achievement resonate with voters, or does a general affordability pitch resonate more?

Both parties are campaigning on the fact that Congress passed major housing legislation with overwhelming bipartisan support. Beyond affordability, another theme in this election is that people want less divisiveness and more collaboration to solve problems. ROAD to Housing was a great example of both parties giving up a few things to get a bill they wanted.

I don’t know that the average voter is digging into a bill with 60 titles, but they understand that Congress recognized a housing supply problem and is at least trying to fix it. If I’m running for Congress, that’s something I’m going to go out and tell people.

Have you noticed more local candidates running explicitly on pro-housing or YIMBY platforms? Any examples?

Our state and local associations make their own endorsements and funding decisions, so, honestly, I’m too far removed to say whether a certain state rep in Texas is doing X.

One interesting part of this election is that the NIMBY focus has shifted from housing to data centers. The recognition that we need more housing has shifted more in the YIMBY direction. That’s a dynamic we’re not encouraging, because data centers are a separate issue, but it’s been interesting.

Talking to our locals, more folks at the city council and county level, where the rubber really meets the road on development, are talking about the need to build more affordable and workforce housing.

We’ve seen in our own polling a real desire, and real angst, from younger voters who feel they can’t afford a home, and from their parents, who are also worried their kids can’t afford a home, may be living with them for a long time, and want them to stay in their state and area and raise their families there. That underlying affordability challenge is driving a lot of the rhetoric and, quite frankly, a lot of the ads. They may not mention housing specifically, but it’s embedded in broader affordability concerns.

You mentioned data centers. I’ve written a couple of stories about data centers competing with housing development for the same land. Is that something NAHB has seen? Is it a real phenomenon?

I think it’s a little overblown, at least right now. A lot of the areas where they’re looking to build data centers aren’t necessarily areas where you would build housing. So there may be some competition over land, but it’s not as big an issue as people may think.

The larger issue is competition for labor. Residential construction always competes with commercial construction for talent and labor, whether it’s somebody building an office building or a house. That competition is real, but it also means more investment in workforce training and more attention to the trades.

We’ve seen many large tech companies announce they’ll fund apprenticeship and training programs because they also need those workers. So there may be some trickle-down help for homebuilding. But it’s still too soon to see real impact, beyond utilities and similar things.

Speaking of labor, I’ve seen quite a few stories about how immigration policy and enforcement have affected construction labor. Has NAHB seen that, what’s your stance, and how have you worked with lawmakers on it?

We’ve definitely heard a lot about it, especially in the last few months. It’s been primarily in Southern states, but not exclusively.

The big concern from members is that the way enforcement is being carried out, whether at the local level, by ICE or some combination, is scaring off all Hispanic workers, regardless of immigration status or citizenship. They’re coming onto job sites, rounding everyone up and detaining folks for hours, repeatedly showing up or pulling people over in a van on the way to a job site. That’s made it very hard to retain workers or get them to show up, because there’s a fear factor in the Hispanic community about even U.S. citizens and green card holders getting roped in with folks who may not be here legally.

That’s caused delays on job sites and made it hard to find labor, period, because there’s no immediate replacement. That’s why we’re so focused on workforce training.

I think it’ll be a factor in places like Texas and Florida, and in the electoral outcome. You’re already seeing Hispanic turnout larger than historic levels. Some polling shows that even folks who supported the president on immigration, who maybe voted for him based on closing the border and enforcement, feel the enforcement has gone too far. It’ll be interesting to see what the exit polls show.

Inman’s core audience is real estate agents. What should agents pay the most attention to in these midterms? Does it depend on their local market, or is there something general to watch?

Disclosure: I used to work for NAR, too, so I understand where they’re coming from. I don’t know if there’s one particular issue, or whether it’s about the House or Senate flipping. It’s the overall voter mindset. If Congress changes control, or a governorship flips one way or the other, does it have an immediate impact? Does it change the [Trump] administration’s course? Those are all open questions.

Ultimately, voters hope inflation can be tamed, and interest rates obviously drive much of this for agents. Resolving the situation in Iran, and maybe dialing back some tariff policies, could affect the inflation numbers driving interest rates. If we can get rates back down, certainly below 7 percent and into the mid-6s, that will unlock a lot of demand that’s still out there but has moved to the sidelines over the last six months.

It’s hard to see how those things will change, no matter the outcome. They all feel very up in the air.

Yeah, but there’s a certain psyche to it. We saw this after the 2024 election. Everyone’s so wrapped up in politics now that people go into a weird holding pattern for the last month or two before an election. They say, “I’m going to wait until after the election and see, and then make a major decision.”

Uncertainty is a factor, and depending on your political outlook, you may be much happier on Nov. 4, or you may not be. But at least it resolves one more question mark for the next two years before we start a presidential cycle.

I hope that, whatever the outcome, having the election behind us will ease angst for potential buyers and sellers, calm the overall market, and get it moving again.

This interview has been edited for length and clarity.

#5576. ePlus Reports Second Quarter and First Half Financial Results Fiscal Year 2027

~ Strong Second Quarter Performance Across Key Metrics ~~ Record Quarterly Gross Billings Exceeded $1 Billion ~~ Increasing Fiscal 2027 Guidance ~

Net sales increased 9.7% to $667.9 million; services revenues decreased 2.4% to $120.8 million.

Gross billings increased 4.3% to $1,066.8 million.

Gross profit increased 11.2% to $180.3 million.

Gross margin was 27.0%, compared to 26.6% for last fiscal year's second quarter.

Net earnings from continuing operations increased 5.8% to $40.4 million.

Adjusted EBITDA increased 14.3% to $67.1 million.

Net earnings from continuing operations per common share-diluted increased 7.6% to $1.56. Non-GAAP: net earnings from continuing operations per common share-diluted increased 19.0% to $1.82.

Net sales increased 5.2% to $1,317.0 million; services revenues remained consistent at $240.2 million.

Gross billings increased 2.5% to $2,023.9 million.

Gross profit increased 5.0% to $331.6 million.

Gross margin remained consistent to last year's first half of 25.2%.

Net earnings from continuing operations increased 0.7% to $70.7 million.

Adjusted EBITDA increased 3.2% to $114.9 million.

Net earnings from continuing operations per common share-diluted increased 2.3% to $2.72. Non-GAAP: net earnings from continuing operations per common share-diluted increased 5.1% to $3.11.

HERNDON, Va., Nov. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- ePlus inc. (NASDAQ: PLUS), a leading provider of technology solutions, today announced financial results for the three months and six months ended September 30, 2026, or the second quarter of its 2027 fiscal year.

"We delivered robust top line growth, improved profitability, and experienced growth against key metrics in the second quarter.  Record gross billings surpassed the prior year's record showing strong momentum reflecting our customer-first approach as we provide the products and services our clients require, particularly for Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Cybersecurity," commented Mark Marron, President and CEO.  "Overall, our solid performance in the second quarter and year to date reflect consistent execution and the strength and breadth of our diversified business model.

"Our strong balance sheet represents a competitive advantage, with our cash position at $381 million at quarter end.  During the second quarter we advanced our acquisition strategy with the purchase of certain assets and liabilities of Daymark Solutions, a provider of critical IT solutions and professional services focused on implementing and supporting complex hybrid cloud, cybersecurity, compliance, and data centers.  We remain disciplined in our approach to capital allocation, balancing acquisitions with other growth investments and returning capital to shareholders via share repurchases and dividend payments."

For the second quarter ended September 30, 2026, as compared to the second quarter ended September 30, 2025:

Net sales increased 9.7% to $667.9 million, from $608.8 million due to higher product sales, partially offset by lower service revenue. Gross billings increased 4.3% to $1,066.8 million from $1,022.7 million.

Product segment sales increased 12.8% to $547.1 million from $485.0 million due to increases in revenue from cloud, security, collaboration and other products, partially offset by a decrease in networking products. Product segment gross margin was 25.8%, up from 24.5% last year due to a shift in product mix, and an increase in sales of third-party maintenance, subscriptions and services that are recognized on a net basis.

Professional services segment revenues decreased 11.3% year over year to $67.8 million from $76.3 million, and gross margin declined to 35.4% from 38.2% during the same period last year due to decreases in revenue and gross profit from project-related services due to delays from retail customers.

Managed services segment revenue increased 11.9% to $53.1 million primarily due to additional revenue from cloud managed services. Gross profit from managed services increased 9.4% year over year due to the increase in revenue, offset by a decrease in gross margin to 28.8% from 29.4% in the prior year quarter.

Gross profit increased 11.2% to $180.3 million, from $162.1 million, due to an increase in gross profit from the product segment and managed services segment, offset by a decrease in the professional services segment. Gross margin was 27.0%, compared with 26.6% in the prior year quarter, due to higher gross margin in the product segment, offset by lower gross margin in the managed services segment and professional services segment.

Operating expenses were $123.8 million, up 9.2% from $113.3 million last year, primarily due to increases in variable compensation commensurate with the increase in gross profit, as well as additional salaries and benefits, general and administrative costs, and expenses related to the acquisition of assets of Daymark Solutions, Inc.("Daymark").

Operating income increased 15.8% to $56.5 million. Other income (expense), net was $(0.5) million compared to $5.2 million in the prior year due to a reduction of $3.5 million in the fair value of the contingent consideration receivable recorded as a result of the sale of our domestic financing business, lower interest income and foreign currency transaction losses being recognized in the current year quarter compared to foreign exchange gains in the prior year quarter. Earnings from continuing operations before taxes increased 3.7% to $56.0 million.

The effective tax rate for the current quarter was 27.9%, which was lower than the prior year quarter of 29.3% primarily due to lower state and local income taxes and lower non-deductible expenses.

Net earnings from continuing operations increased 5.8% to $40.4 million from $38.2 million in the prior year quarter. Adjusted EBITDA increased 14.3% to $67.1 million from $58.7 million in the prior year quarter. Net earnings from continuing operations per common share-diluted was $1.56, up from $1.45 in the prior year quarter. Non-GAAP net earnings from continuing operations per common share diluted was $1.82, compared with $1.53 in the prior year quarter. Total shares outstanding were 26.0 million and 26.3 million on September 30, 2026, and March 31, 2026, respectively.

Net earnings were $40.4 million as compared to $34.9 million in the prior year quarter. Last year, earnings from discontinued operations, net of taxes, for the three months ended September 30, 2025, was a loss of $3.3 million and net (loss) from discontinued operations per common share diluted for the three months ended September 30, 2025, was $(0.13). There were no transactions for discontinued operations for the three months ended September 30, 2026.

For the six months ended September 30, 2026, as compared to the six months ended September 30, 2025:

Net sales increased 5.2% to $1,317.0 million, from $1,251.6 million due to higher product sales. Gross billings increased 2.5% to $2,023.9 million from $1,975.4 million.

Product segment sales increased 6.5% to $1,076.7 million from $1,011.4 million due to increases in revenue from cloud, security, and collaboration products, offset by a decrease in networking products.  Product segment gross margin was 23.4%, up from 22.8% last year due to a shift in product mix, and an increase in sales of third-party maintenance and subscriptions.

Professional services segment revenues decreased 8.3% year over year to $135.8 million from $148.1 million, and gross margin declined to 36.2% from 38.7% during the same period last year, both primarily due to decreases in revenue from project services, and staff augmentation.

Managed services segment revenue increased 13.4% to $104.4 million primarily due to additional sales of cloud services. Gross profit from managed services segment increased 10.3% year on year due to the increase in revenue, offset by a decline in gross margin to 29.1% from 29.9%, mainly driven by increased third-party costs.

Gross profit increased 5.0% to $331.6 million, from $315.8 million due to an increase in gross profit from the product segment and managed services segment, offset by a decrease in the professional services segment. Gross margin remained consistent at 25.2%, compared to the six-month period in the prior year.

Operating expenses were $236.3 million, up 5.5% from $224.0 million last year, primarily due to increases in variable compensation commensurate with the increase in gross profit, as well as additional salaries and benefits, general and administrative costs, and expenses related to the acquisition of assets of Daymark.

Operating income increased 3.9% to $95.4 million. Other income (expense), net was $2.6 million compared to $5.8 million last year, due to the reduction of contingent consideration receivable of $3.5 million, offset by decreased foreign exchange losses and increased interest income during the current six-month period. Earnings from continuing operations before taxes increased 0.4% to $98.0 million.

The effective tax rate for the six months ended September 30, 2026, was 27.9%, which was lower than the same six-month period in the prior year of 28.1% primarily due to state and local taxes and lower non-deductible expenses.

Net earnings from continuing operations increased 0.7% to $70.7 million from $70.2 million in the prior year. Adjusted EBITDA increased 3.2% to $114.9 million from $111.4 million in the prior year six-month period. Net earnings from continuing operations per common share-diluted was $2.72, compared with $2.66 in the prior year. Non-GAAP: Net earnings from continuing operations per common share-diluted was $3.11, compared with $2.96 in the prior year.

Net earnings were $70.7 million as compared to $77.4 million in the prior year. Earnings from discontinued operations, net of taxes, for the six months ended September 30, 2025, was $7.3 million. Net earnings from discontinued operations per common share - diluted for the six months ended September 30, 2025, was $0.28. There were no transactions for discontinued operations for the six months ended September 30, 2026.

As of September 30, 2026, cash and cash equivalents were $380.9 million, down from $410.8 million as of March 31, 2026. Inventory increased 35.1% to $271.4 million as of September 30, 2026, compared with $200.9 million as of March 31, 2026, due to several ongoing projects. Accounts receivableâtrade, net increased 14.9% to $746.9 million as of September 30, 2026 from $650.0 million as of March 31, 2026. Total stockholders' equity was $1,096.4 million as of September 30, 2026, compared with $1,069.0 million as of March 31, 2026.

ePlus is increasing its fiscal year 2027 guidance of year over year growth to the upper single digits for net sales and gross profit, and the low double digits for adjusted EBITDA.

This guidance does not factor in recessionary conditions, or other unexpected developments.  ePlus cannot predict with reasonable certainty and without unreasonable effort, the ultimate outcome of unusual gains and losses, the occurrence of matters creating GAAP tax impacts, fluctuations in interest expense or interest income and share-based compensation, and acquisition- or disposition-related expenses. These items are uncertain, depend on various factors, and could be material to ePlus' results computed in accordance with GAAP. Accordingly, ePlus is unable to provide a reconciliation of GAAP net earnings from continuing operations to Adjusted EBITDA for the full fiscal year 2027 forecast.

ePlus announced today that its Board of Directors has declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.27 per common share which will be paid on December 16, 2026, to shareholders of record as of the close of business on November 24, 2026.

"The accelerating adoption of AI, increasing demand for advanced data center infrastructure and growing emphasis on cybersecurity and digital transformation continue to reshape the technology landscape, creating significant opportunities for long-term growth for ePlus.  As organizations accelerate investments in modernizing their IT networks and strengthening cybersecurity, our deep customer relationships and broad portfolio of products and services position us well to meet demand and support our customers' growth.  These factors, combined with our strong performance year to date, support our confidence in the sustainability of our business trends and our increased full year fiscal 2027 guidance," concluded Mr. Marron.

#5575. Why real estate agents wanted Barbara Corcoran for ICNY ’27

Barbara Corcoran (l) onstage at Inman Connect San Francisco 2015, Holly Meyer Lucas (r) onstage at Inman Connect San Diego 2026 |

As our team at Inman began planning Inman Connect New York this January, we asked real estate agents a fairly straightforward question: “In this market, who do you want to hear from most right now?”

The overwhelming response was Barbara Corcoran.

I’ve spent a lot of time thinking about that answer, because I think it tells us something interesting about the current state of real estate, the people who work in it and what they’re looking for from our industry’s leaders.

For context, before becoming Inman’s CMO, I spent years building a $100 million-plus producing real estate team in South Florida. I’ve personally sold more than 1,000 homes, ranging from properties under $20,000 to deals north of $20 million.

I’ve represented distressed sellers, helped families through extraordinarily difficult circumstances and negotiated transactions where getting to the closing table meant everything to the people involved. I’ve also mentored, trained and managed hundreds of agents through slow markets, busy markets and everything the last decade has thrown at us.

My point: I’ve carried the bag, and I understand my real estate agent brethren.

So, all summer when agents told me how much they are struggling (in what should be peak homebuying season), I took that seriously. For the past several months, I’ve heard from some of the most successful agents in the country who were going months without closing a transaction. These are experienced professionals who have built substantial businesses and survived multiple market cycles, suddenly finding themselves in unfamiliar territory.

Meanwhile, the industry around them is in a rather extraordinary state of upheaval. Major brokerages are consolidating, brokerages and MLSs are suing one another, the debate over private listings continues to divide the industry, and NAR is working to rebuild trust following several tumultuous years.

And somewhere in the middle of all this, agents are trying to sell houses while being told to post more on social media, stay hydrated and use more AI.

Our industry has some consequential decisions ahead of it, and the people making those decisions deserve to be questioned. Inman’s newsroom has an important responsibility to cover these issues, and our events should provide a place for the people involved to explain their positions.

But there’s another conversation agents want to have, and I think their overwhelming request for Barbara tells us exactly what it is.

They want to hear from someone who has been in their shoes, knows how to get scrappy in a down market to sell real estate, and can offer an experienced perspective without having to defend a corporate agenda.

One of my favorite anecdotes about Barbara is one that she shares often and seems to take enormous pride in — how gritty she was in her early life. Her LinkedIn bio opens with: “Barbara Corcoran’s credits include straight D’s in high school and college and 20 jobs by the time she turned 23.”

Tell me that doesn’t win the heart of a real estate agent. Our industry has a remarkable way of attracting people who struggled to find their place elsewhere.

Some weren’t great students. Others bounced around between jobs before finding real estate. I’ve met extraordinarily successful agents who can negotiate their way through an impossible transaction, recognize an opportunity before anyone else and build a relationship with practically anyone, and yet were kicked out of school when they were younger. (Looking at you, James Harris!)

Barbara herself has spoken openly about her struggles in school and dyslexia and how the challenges she experienced influenced the way she approached business. (I’ve got a completely unscientific theory about how I think many of America’s top-producing real estate agents who claim they struggled in school but are elite at selling are all actually just dyslexic, but I’ll save that for another time.)

Real estate agents find Barbara’s story particularly inspiring because real estate has always been an industry where people can build extraordinary careers around abilities that aren’t necessarily rewarded in a classroom, and Barbara took those abilities and turned a $1,000 loan into one of the most recognizable real estate brokerages in the country. She is one of us, and she made it out on the other side a literal Shark. And agents love her for it.

To boot, she built The Corcoran Group in New York City, where competition was fierce and standing out required creativity — something agents covet and understand deeply. Long before agents were being told to become content creators, Barbara understood how to make herself and her business interesting to the public. She launched market reports, generated publicity and became a recognizable authority on New York real estate.

She understood personal brand marketing before most of our industry knew what to call it.

She sold her brokerage in 2001 and went on to build another career as an entrepreneur, investor and television personality. And now, after all of that, there she is sitting in a chair on Shark Tank, evaluating other entrepreneurs and deciding which businesses deserve her money.

Barbara understands something that most successful real estate agents figure out, and the new ones need to hear: A willingness to take risks, build relationships and solve problems can take you a very long way in this business.

And she’s spent enough time carrying the bag to know how to find business when everyone else is convinced there isn’t any. Her perspective on this is particularly valuable for agents to hear, if we consider the voices dominating our industry’s conversations right now.

The real estate conversations are dominated by brokerage executives defending their business models, MLS leaders explaining their policies and industry organizations navigating enormous changes; senators are filing FTC complaints against industry leaders, too. It’s overwhelming, and yet, none of it helps Susie Realtor or Mike Agent close a home this quarter.

There are important questions being debated about how homes should be marketed, who controls listing information, and how real estate professionals will operate in the years ahead, and while I do believe all of those discussions deserve a place on highly influential stages such as Inman Connect New York, agents also desperately need to hear from voices right now who don’t have a dog in the fight, who can hunker down on a mic and say, “OK, listen up, this is exactly what I would do right now if I were in your shoes.”

Barbara Corcoran is the real estate fairy godmother who is uniquely positioned to say that, without an obvious bias, something to sell the audience or any other ulterior motive. That dynamic really appeals to agents right now, who are growing tired of the industry’s constant infighting.

A real estate agent trying to figure out how to get their listing sold after sitting for 90-plus days, so they can get their client the win and feed their own family, is less concerned with which brokerage executive launches their AI tool most effectively and who is winning the latest argument about private listings.

Agents need a change of scenery right now, and Barbara knows how to generate business, find the buyer and create buzz around listings that have been sitting for weeks.

She’s also famously candid, and I suspect she will have plenty to say about what is happening in our industry.

My takeaway from the overwhelming request for Barbara is that agents are craving an independent voice of reason. Someone who understands the realities of selling real estate and can speak from experience.

And when our community made that request, we listened.

I want to give credit to Inman CEO Tom Bohn for taking the feedback seriously and making Barbara a priority for New York. One of the things I’ve appreciated about working with Tom is his willingness to listen to the real estate professionals who make up our community with fresh perspectives, while also prioritizing the industry leadership who are critical to our ecosystem as an industry.

We have an opportunity to put some of the smartest people in the business on our stages. I think we should pay particular attention when the people in our audience tell us whose perspective they value.

So, we got Barbara, and she’s going to tell our audience exactly what she would do right now. And we can’t wait to hear it.

Join us at Inman Connect New York, Jan. 26–28, 2027, at the New York Hilton Midtown.

#5574. Box taps Nvidia’s AI models to build a rich context layer for autonomous enterprise agents

Few technology firms have embraced the arrival of artificial intelligence agents quite like Box Inc., and today it went even further down the road to automation with an expanded partnership with Nvidia Corp.

At its annual customer conference BoxWorks 2026, Box debuted a new retrieval engine that’s powered by Nvidia’s AI models and designed to give AI agents the much-needed context they require to get more work done. It was announced alongside a new orchestration tool for multistep agentic workflows and new threat detection tools designed to safeguard organizations from rogue agents.

Box’s flurry of announcements are designed to fix a growing bottleneck in enterprise AI workflows. As Box Chief Executive Aaron Levie explained, autonomous agents are only as useful as the context they’re fed allows them to be. If AI agents lack context, they’re going to make mistakes, and that means enterprises simply won’t trust them to do any work, stalling adoption.

Levie said that much of the context that AI agents need does not reside in clean, structured databases, but rather deep inside organizations’ messy troves of unstructured data – things such as contracts, software documentation, policy manuals, internal emails, customer communications records and research archives. Companies know that’s the case, but they’re wary about letting autonomous agents jump right into their data. What’s needed is a way to give those agents secure, permission-aware access to this data, so they’re not looking at things they’re not authorized to see or accidentally leaking secrets all over the internet.

This is where Box’s new partnership with Nvidia intends to make a difference. The company today introduced a new tool called Box Content Retrieval, which is a data retrieval engine that transforms messy enterprise content into a structured knowledge base that agents can access more easily and reason over. It was built using Nvidia’s specialized Nemotron Retriever embedding models, which help to create a neat index of unstructured content like scanned documents, images, audio and video files using multimodal and hybrid search techniques.

Box said Box Content Retrieval is able to improve search accuracy by 20% while reducing token consumption by up to 90%, enabling AI agents to find the context they need to improve their response times to worker’s questions by around four-times. It also makes sure that each AI agent adheres to the native file permissions for each piece of content, so they’re never able to access files their users don’t have permission to see.

“By partnering with Nvidia we are creating a new intelligence layer for enterprise content that gives customers faster, more precise ways to ground AI in the content that powers their business,” Levie said.

The new partnership also sees Box bringing Nvidia’s frontier open-weight models to the table, including the new Nemotron 3 Ultra large language model. These models are directly available within Box AI, and because they’re open-weight, they can be accessed at much more affordable prices than proprietary models from companies like Anthropic PBC and OpenAI Group PBC.

Nvidia’s open-weight models have been trained on the domain-specific knowledge for highly specialized workflows, Levie said. For instance, financial analysts can use Nemotron Ultra 3 to query loan applications with strict data-access boundaries, while legal teams can use it to identify contract precedents within corporate agreements by understanding their conceptual meaning rather than searching for keyword matches.

“Open weight is an important part of our vision, complementing closed models while driving innovation and broader adoption across the industry,” Levie added.

Holger Mueller of Constellation Research told SiliconANGLE that Box’s partnership with Nvidia bodes well for the company because the chipmaker is by far and away still the world’s leader in AI platforms, and it will allow it to integrate more closely with the leading public cloud providers too. “Documents are a treasure trove for AI in general and context specifically, and enterprises are very keen to tap into them so they can develop better AI applications,” the analyst said. “This confirms the theory that data has to move to the compute in the AI era.”

Box’s AI push isn’t totally reliant on Nvidia. Indeed, it has its own thing going on with Box Architect, a new tool that will launch in beta later this year, allowing business workers to build, test and deploy new agentic processes using their natural language. According to Box, it can connect to native Box tools such as Extract, Automate, Apps and Forms to create complex workflows, with a selection of open and closed models.

Using Box Architect, law firms will be able to build contract review workflows that are informed by their previously-approved playbooks for past agreements, so that they can compare incoming contracts against it. Should it flag any high-risk clauses, these can immediately be sent to an attorney for review. Alternatively, a bank might use Box Architect to build a streamlined client onboarding workflow that collects applications through Forms, verifies identity documents with Extract and then generates and signs an agreement with Doc Gen and Sign.

Deep Analysis analyst Alan Pelz-Sharpe said these are the kinds of coordinated, autonomous workflows that can make a real difference in terms of the value enterprise AI provides. “While legacy approaches require brittle point-to-point configurations for extraction and execution, an integrated agentic design layer dynamically orchestrates content understanding, process steps and analytical visualization within a single governed ecosystem,” he said.

Box also understands that organizations are going to need more security to protect these more advanced and capable AI agents, which is why it’s simultaneously introducing new threat detection capabilities across its platform. The company said the new security tools make it possible to identify the actions of rogue AI agents in real-time, so that if any of them start exfiltrating data in bulk, deleting massive numbers of files, or taking over user accounts, they’ll immediately be flagged for review.

For instance, administrators will be able to control what files each agent can access through classification-based policies, constrain agent’s actions with MCP guardrails that dictate which third-party tools each one can use, and then detect harmful activities that exceed predefined limits.

#5573. Applied Optoelectronics Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results

SUGAR LAND, Texas, Nov. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Applied Optoelectronics, Inc. (NASDAQ: AAOI) ("AOI"), a leading provider of advanced optical and HFC networking products that power AI, today announced financial results for its third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

"We are pleased to have generated record revenue for our sixth consecutive quarter and to have returned to GAAP profitability in Q3," said Dr. Thompson Lin, AOI's Founder, President and Chief Executive Officer. "We have made meaningful progress in scaling our manufacturing capabilities, particularly for our 800G and 1.6T products, to address demand for AI-related optical technologies that we believe is accelerating. We have recently secured a multi-year strategic agreement with a Tier 1 hyperscale datacenter customer, which we think provides us with improved long-term visibility and reinforces our confidence in the opportunity ahead as demand for high-bandwidth, energy-efficient optical connectivity products continues to grow."

"We delivered another solid quarter, including accelerating revenue growth and improving profitability, driven by robust demand and manufacturing expansion in both our datacenter and CATV businesses," said Dr. Stefan Murry, AOI's Chief Financial Officer and Chief Strategy Officer. "We currently have a total manufacturing equipment capacity approaching 330,000 units per month. We expect our 2027 capacity expansion plan in the US to take longer to complete due to longer than expected time to obtain necessary electrical power among other construction related issues. As we work through these construction issues, we now expect by the end of 2026 that we will have sufficient manufacturing equipment installed to produce over 500,000 pieces of 800G and 1.6 Tb products per month and we expect to grow our manufacturing capacity to over 1 million pieces of 800G and 1.6 Tb transceivers per month by the end of 2027. We remain focused on executing on our capacity expansion plans and believe we are well positioned to support the next phase of AI datacenter deployment."
